title: Untensored base change for an arbitrary scheme over the field
statement:
Let $K$ be a field. Let $Z$ and $S'$ be $K$-schemes and let $g:T\to S'$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism. Put $X'=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}S'$ and $Y=X'\times_{S'}T$, with projections $p:X'\to Z$, $f':X'\to S'$, $h:Y\to X'$ and $e:Y\to T$. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $K$. For every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, the canonical map
$$(f')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F\longrightarrow Rh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$$
is an isomorphism in $D^+(X'_{\mathrm{et}},\mathbf F_\ell)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The map is the $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$-adjoint of $e^{-1}g^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{e^{-1}\varepsilon_g}e^{-1}\mathcal F$, using $h^{-1}(f')^{-1}=e^{-1}g^{-1}$ and the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. No finite-type hypothesis on $Z$, $S'$ or $T$ is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0F1I and 0EZT, arbitrary-scheme extension in the proof of Tag 0F1J

proof.text: Take the affine cover U_i of Z and pull it back to X=Z×_K S′. Its maps a_i are etale by pullback stability. They are jointly surjective: choose a preimage of the Z-coordinate in an affine chart, then lift the compatible pair through the scheme pullback. Apply the source library theorem Etale.isIso_baseChange_app_of_etale_cover (the module-coefficient bounded-below implementation of etale locality), using V_i=S′, T_i=T and identity cover maps on both.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, first paragraph of proof; Tag 0EZT, assertion (2)

proof.text: On each affine chart, use the exact coefficient-forgetting exchange theorem. Every section of the underlying module is killed by ell; stalk functors are additive, so the same holds on all geometric stalks, with ell positive and invertible in K. Apply the affine abelian base-change theorem. Transport along the forgetful functor’s single-object comparison and reflect invertibility. The identity inverse-image comparison identifies the local input objects with F[0], completing the locality argument.

from.place: the arbitrary-scheme extension of the untensored base-change assertion, using affine finitely generated subalgebras and the 0EZT limit comparison

split_report.summary: Extended the existing finite-type-over-K abelian 0F1I theorem to arbitrary Z using affine opens, finitely generated K-subalgebras, Spec/limit and fibre-product continuity, and the existing 0EZT comparison. Explicitly checked coefficient forgetting, injective restriction and canonical exchange compatibility. No new nodes and no statement change. Corrected the source location: the affine approximation paragraph is in the proof of 0F1I, used by 0F1J. Maintainer reader (Q43 review): added the termwise-exchange citation in Step 2 and the unbounded/bounded-below exchange agreement in Step 5.
split_report.blueprint: lem-kun-0f1j.proof.md, last finite-pushforward paragraph: removes the unjustified assertion that every finite cover X_i of an arbitrary affine X is finite type over K, by proving the arbitrary-scheme untensored input via the first paragraph of Stacks 0F1I. This is the precise place recorded in blueprint.from.place.

tool_uses.why: Forgets constant module coefficients while identifying the canonical exchange; the unit has no coefficient-forgetting theorem.
Exactness of abelian inverse image, used to restrict resolutions and identify negative cohomology; generic site tool.
Restriction to an etale open preserves injective resolutions; generic site tool absent from this unit.
Identifies the canonical open-square exchange termwise; generic site localization tool.
Converts the subalgebra colimit to the inverse limit of affine schemes; a generic algebraic geometry tool.
Provides affine transitions and the two product-limit identifications needed to apply the unit's 0EZT theorem.
Detects isomorphisms by cohomology in the full bounded-below subcategory; generic derived-category tool.
Identifies the derived exchange of the open restriction square with the termwise underived exchange on an injective resolution; generic exchange tool, the unit has no such statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q43-114b5b0a5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and all seven steps, every cited statement, and Stacks etale-cohomology.tex at lemma-punctual-base-change (0F1I) proof paragraph 1, lemma-base-change-Rf-star-colim (0EZT)(2) and the start of the 0F1J proof. The statement is 0F1I for an arbitrary K-scheme Z, specialised to F_ell coefficients with ell invertible in K, which is exactly how the parent lem-kun-0f1j uses it (its Step 4). The map is the F_ell-linear mate in D^+. Edge cases Z empty, F=0, Z=Spec K and B=K[t1,t2,...] are all consistent. The route follows 0F1I paragraph 1: reduce to affine Z, write it as a limit of finite-type Spec B_i, apply lem-kun-0f1i to each, then pass to the limit with lem-kun-0ezt. Every hypothesis holds: the index set is directed and nonempty, all transitions are affine, g is qcqs, and A is ell-torsion. There are no new nodes, no duplicate (I grepped 0F1I and punctual-base-change), no cycle and no SGA. I fixed two missing citations (C1/C3/C4). (1) Step 2 went from 'the termwise underived exchange is an isomorphism' to 'the derived open exchange is an isomorphism' without a cited statement. It now cites lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise with J=j_Y^{-1}I, which is K-injective by lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative. The termwise lemma is declared as a tool use. (2) Step 5 treated lem-kun-0f1i's unbounded exchange (def-kun-unbounded-exchange) as the bounded-below exchange of def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange. It now cites lem-kun-unbounded-exchange-agrees and the fullness of D^+ in D (def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories). I accepted the declared tool_uses (coefficient forgetting, inverse-image exactness, injective restriction, underived open exchange, Spec/limit, product limits, cohomology criterion) plus the added termwise lemma. Statement unchanged.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
